Navigate to iCloud > iWriter. Press Select and choose the document. Press the Versions button located on the top navigation bar. How to discover keyboard shortcuts on iPad? Attach the external keyboard to iPad. Tap the editor’s field. Press and hold the command button (⌘). Does iWriter support RTF? iWriter doesn’t have RTF support. You can use iWriter Pro for Mac to export your documents as RTF. Is there a Mac version? iWriter doesn’t have a Mac version. iWriter Pro has both iOS and Mac versions. I have another question… If you have a question that is not covered here, contact us and we’ll answer as best as we can. We take a break on the weekends, but during weekdays we aim to reply within 1–2 business days. Please note that the more detailed your description is, the quicker and better we can answer. The device model, correct app name, OS version, or screenshots will also help a lot.

content:
What is the difference between iWriter and iWriter Pro? The Pro features, such as: Markdown editing and preview, Math formula support, and many others. Does iWriter Pro have an URL scheme? For now, x-callback-url schemes are not supported. How can I save my document? I can't find a save button. iWriter Pro implements autosave. You should not care about document saving. All changes are saved automatically. I want to know more about MultiMarkdown. Great! Please follow this link to MultiMarkdown Syntax Guide. Does iWriter Pro support RTF? You can use iWriter Pro for Mac to export your documents as RTF. Is automatic light/dark theme switching supported? Yes. Automatic theme switching works in tandem with the system’s appearance settings. iWriter Pro “memorizes” chosen themes for both system appearance modes (Light and Dark). For manual appearance selection please navigate to:
On iOS: Settings > Display & Brightness. On Mac: System Preferences > General > Appearance. How can I restore a previous version of a document? You can do that for iCloud documents. To browse document versions:
Navigate to iCloud > iWriter Pro. Press Select button and choose the document. Press the Versions button located on the top navigation bar. How to discover keyboard shortcuts on iPad? Attach an external keyboard to the iPad (e.g. Apple Magic Keyboard). Tap the editor’s field. Press and hold the command button (⌘). How to find the Word Counter and Shortcuts menus on iPad? Word Counter and Shortcuts are located on the system keyboard.
Enable the Autocorrection option in Settings > Text Editing. Begin editing text. The required buttons will be located in the top right corner. How to open a split-screen on iPad? iWriter Pro supports the multi-window mode starting with iOS 13. You can use this feature to edit a Markdown document and observe its Preview at the same time.
Open two copies of iWriter Pro on iPad. Open the same document on the left and on the right. Activate Preview in any window. The Preview gets automatically updated when you edit the document. What about Dropbox support? You will need the Dropbox app (on iOS and Mac) to be able to open and edit files stored there. The same goes for Google Drive and other 3rd-party storage providers. Please note, some developers have incomplete support of iOS protocols; therefore, you may be missing some features. I cannot insert image from the Photo Library on iOS. Use iWriter Pro’s folders when inserting images. Importing images from Photo Library or Camera saves them next to the document. iOS sandboxes restrict access to 3rd-party folders. To fix this, copy your document to any iWriter Pro folder (local or iCloud). I get an error message when trying to rename a document. Files outside iWriter Pro’s folders can’t be renamed from within the editor due to iOS security restrictions. Privacy settings can’t lift this issue. iWriter Pro has full access to its local and iCloud folders, which can be found by the app icon.
Rename files from within the Document Menu. Tap and hold a file, then choose Rename.
Is there a Mac version? iWriter Pro for Mac is available here. Where can I find privacy policy for iWriter Pro? You can read it here. I have another question… If you have a question that is not covered here, contact us and we’ll answer as best as we can. We take a break on the weekends, but during weekdays we aim to reply within 1-2 business days. Please note that the more detailed your description is, the quicker and better we can answer. The device model, correct app name, OS version, or screenshots will also help a lot. I have a feature request… You can send your request via e-mail here. Please note that not all features can be added to the final product. Leaving a one-star comment on the App Store while asking for a feature has never helped anyone.

title: MultiMarkdown Syntax Guide

content:
Everything you can type in iWriter 2: the Markdown you write, and what it turns into. Copy any example into a document to try it.
Headings: To create a heading, add one to six # symbols before your heading text. The number of # you use will determine the hierarchy level and typeface size of the heading.
Text styling: Wrap words in symbols to make them bold, italic, crossed out or highlighted.
Paragraphs and line breaks: A blank line starts a new paragraph. To break a line inside a paragraph, end it with two spaces, a backslash or <br/>.
Blockquotes: Start a line with > to quote it. Use >> to quote inside a quote.
Lists: Start lines with -, * or + for unordered lists, or with numbers for ordered lists. Indent a line to nest it under the one above.
Horizontal rules: Put three or more of the same symbol on a line of its own to draw a rule. iWriter 2 supports four delimiter styles.
Escaped characters: Precede a symbol with a backslash to display it as typed rather than using it for formatting.
Links: You can create an inline link by wrapping link text in brackets [ ], and then wrapping the URL in parentheses ( ).
Wikilinks: Link to another document in iWriter 2 by its name, in double square brackets.
Images: You can display an image by adding ! and wrapping the alt text in [ ]. Alt text is a short text equivalent of the information in the image. Then, wrap the link for the image in parentheses ( ).
Image embeds: Show a picture from your folders with ![[ ]]. You can change the image dimensions by adding |200x100 to the link, where 200 is the width and 100 is the height.
Tables: Separate columns with | and put a line of dashes under the header. Colons in that line align the columns.
Footnotes: Add [^name] where the note belongs, and write the note anywhere in the document.
Definition lists: Put a term on one line and its definition on the next, after a colon and spaces.
Cross-references: Link to a heading by its text in square brackets, or by an id you give it.
Table of contents: Use the {{TOC}} shortcut for a table of contents.
Page break: Use 5 or more plus symbols + to add a page break.
Document metadata: Put Key: value lines at the very top of the document. They are used when you export, for example as the title and author of a PDF or EPUB.
Code: Wrap code in backticks inside a sentence. For a block of code, indent every line with a tab or four spaces, or use a fenced block.
HTML: Plain HTML works too, and a <style> block changes how the preview and exports look.
Math: Write math in LaTeX between $ signs inside a sentence, or between $$ lines for a block.
Diagrams: Draw flowcharts, sequence diagrams, timelines and more with Mermaid.
Insert other documents: Put the text of another document into the edited one, with MultiMarkdown or wikilink syntax.
Citations: Cite a source with [#name] and list it anywhere in the document. A page number can go first.
Abbreviations: Define an abbreviation with [>…].
Glossary: Mark a term with [?…] to define it. The definitions are collected in a glossary.
Subscript and superscript: ^ raises the characters after it and ~ lowers them.

content:
This is the legacy version of MMD Guide. If you are looking for iWriter 2 version, please go here Headings # To create a heading, add one to six # symbols before your heading text. The number of # you use will determine the hierarchy level and typeface size of the heading.
ATX-Style Headings
# This is a heading H1 ## This is a heading H2 ### This is a heading H3 #### This is a heading H4 ##### This is a heading H5 ###### This is a heading H6 # Heading with custom id [custom-id] Setext Headings are also supported:
A First Level Header ========= A Second Level Header --------- Text Styling # Strong style
This text is **bold**. This text is also __bold__. Emphasis style
This text is *italicized*. This text is also _italicized_. Oblique style
This text is ***oblique***. This text is also ___oblique___. Strikethrough style
And this is the ~~strikethrough~~ style. Lists # You can make an unordered list by preceding one or more lines of text with -, *, or +.
* Bulleted list item + Bulleted list item - Bulleted list item To order your list, precede each line with a number.
1. Numbered list item 2. Numbered list item 3. Numbered list item To create a task list, preface list items with a hyphen and space followed by [ ]. To mark a task as complete, use [x].
- [ ] Task list item - [ ] Task list item - [x] Task list item Nested Lists # You can create a nested list by indenting one or more list items below another item.
1. First list item - First nested list item - Second nested list item Links # [Link Title](/url/to/destination) [iwriter](https://serpensoft.com/iwriter-2/) If your URL contains blank spaces, you must escape them by replacing them with %20.
[Optional Link Title](/url%20with%20spaces) Inline links:
<foo@example.com> Link to <http://serpensoft.com> Reference-style link:
Link to [Website][Link]. ... [Link]: http://serpensoft.com Reference link with styling:
Link to [Website]. ... [Website]: http://serpensoft.com style="border: solid black 1px;" Images # You can display an image by adding ! and wrapping the alt text in [ ]. Alt text is a short text equivalent of the information in the image. Then, wrap the link for the image in parentheses ().
![Optional Caption](/link/to/image "Optional title") Inline image:
![image](Website.png "This is a title") Image with attributes:
![image] ... [image]: Website.png "This is a title" height=25px width=50px Image by itself becomes a figure:
![This is the caption][image] [image]: Website.png "This is the title" height=45px width=120px Block-quotes # You can quote text with a >.
Regular text. > Blockquote > with two lines. And one more line. >> And a second level blockquote. Paragraphs and Line Breaks # To create a line break in a Markdown file, you will need to include one of the following:
Include two spaces at the end of the first line.
This example Will span two lines. Include a backslash at the end of the first line.
This example\ Will span two lines. Include an HTML single line break tag at the end of the first line.
This example<br/> Will span two lines. Or, leave a blank line between two lines.
This example Will span two lines. Code Blocks # This is an inline code block.
Indent text with tabs or 4+ space characters to create a multiline code block:
This is a longer section of code on multiple lines. Fenced Code Blocks # ``` This is a fenced code block. ``` Fenced code block with a language marker:
```perl print "Hello, world!\n"; $a = 0; while ($a < 10) { print "$a...\n"; $a++; } ``` Footnotes # Reference style:
Text[^foot]. [^foot]: This is a footnote. Inline:
Text[^This is an inline footnote.]. Horizontal rule # ----- - - - - - ***** * * * * * Tables # Simple table:
| foo | bar | | --- | --- | | foo | bar | | foo bar || [*caption*][id] Table with aligned columns:
| right aligned | centered | left aligned | | ---: | :---: | :--- | | foo | bar | bat | | foo | bar | bat | [*caption*][id] HTML Blocks # The app supports plain HTML blocks.
<p>This is HTML paragraph.</p> <mark>This text is highlighted.</mark> You can also modify the underlying styling using CSS:
<style> p { color: yellow; } </style> Blank lines within tags are not supported. Page Break # Use this code snippet to insert a page break:
<div style='break-after:page'></div> Math and Diagrams # You can add math expressions to your notes using MathJax and the LaTeX notation.
Inline math:
$e^{2i\pi} = 1$ Math block:
$$ \begin{vmatrix}a & b\\ c & d \end{vmatrix}=ad-bc $$ You can add diagrams and charts to your notes, using Mermaid. Mermaid supports a range of diagrams, such as flow charts, sequence diagrams, and timelines.
```mermaid sequenceDiagram Alice->>+John: Hello John, how are you? Alice->>+John: John, can you hear me? John-->>-Alice: Hi Alice, I can hear you! John-->>-Alice: I feel great! ``` Table of contents # Use this shortcut to generate the document’s table of contents:
{{TOC}} The table of contents will be automatically generated from the available headings.
Insert other documents (transclusion) # Use the following syntax to attach the content of external document:
{{filename.md}} {{folder/filename.md}} {{folder/filename with spaces.md}} Citations # Reference style:
Cite a source.[p. 42][#source] [#source]: John Doe. *A Totally Fake Book*. Vanity Press, 2006. Inline:
Cite a source.[p. 42][#John Doe. *A Totally Fake Book*. Vanity Press, 2006.] Cross-references # # Intro # # Conclusion [fin] # Link to [Intro]. Link to the [end][fin]. Definition Lists # Apple : Pomaceous fruit of plants of the genus Malus in the family Rosaceae. Also the makers of really great products. Abbreviations # Reference style:
HTML and HTML [>HTML]: Hypertext Markup Language Inline:
[>(HTML) Hypertext Markup Language] and HTML Glossary # Reference style:
[?Glossary] is a glossary term. [?Glossary]: The glossary collects information about important terms used in your document. Inline:
[?(Glossary) The glossary collects information about important terms used in your document] is a glossary term. Subscript & Superscript # m2
m^2 x2y3
x^2 y^3 xz
x~z C6H12O6
C~6~H~12~O~6~ Escaped characters # \& \$ \* \_ Document Metadata # Metadata fields should be added at the top of the document.
Title: This is a title Author: John Appleseed E-Mail: email@server.com Date: 2025-10-20 Metadata will be applied during the export process.
Acknowledgements # MultiMarkdown Syntax Guide by Fletcher T. Penney.

Improvements for scrolling in Split mode. Fixed bugs with attached external files and images. Fixed bug with HTML comment highlighting. 4.1 # Added syntax highlighting for LaTeX notations. Performance optimization for Split mode. Editor should be much more responsive during text editing. Fixed bugs with attached external files and images. Fixed various bugs in user interface. The backslash line-break symbol is now colorized. 4.0 # New Dashboard panel with Navigation and Text Statistics. German and Russian localizations added. Preview plugins updated: Mermaid (8.13.4), Flowchart (1.17.0), Highlight.js (11.3.1). Fixed issues with export to DOCX format. Fixed various issues in Focus mode. Various bug fixes and performance improvements. iWriter Pro now requires MacOS 11 or higher. 3.5 # QuickLook plugins for preview and thumbnails updated. It is now possible to navigate with keyboard keys in HTML preview. Fixed issues with export to DOCX format. Fixed issues with export to LaTeX format. Fixed highlighting for strikethrough elements containing sub-items. Fixed highlighting for multi-line Math elements. Mermaid plugin updated to the version 8.12.0. Other minor bug fixes and improvements. 3.4 # QuickLook plugins for preview and thumbnails updated. It is now possible to navigate with keyboard keys in HTML preview. Fixed issues with the behavior of paragraph spacing option. Fixed issues with inserting references to images and external files. Fixed highlighting for strikethrough elements containing sub-items. Fixed highlighting for multi-line Math elements. Mermaid plugin updated to the version 8.12.0. Other minor bug fixes and improvements. 3.3 # Editor’s rendering system updated. Improved text layout and cursor positioning. Maximum available line height value increased. Header labels are now rendered with dimmed colors. Other bug fixes and improvements. 3.2 # Mermaid plugin updated to the version 8.10.2. MathJax plugin updated to the version 3.2.0. Highlight.js plugin updated to the version 11.0.1. Fixed formatting for tabulated lists. Text font size and Preview font scale can now be changed via keyboard shortcuts independently. List insert/remove actions now respect spacing at the start of the line. Preview now supports magnification when using trackpad pinch-to-zoom gesture. QuickLook plugin updated. 3.1 # Fixed issues with inconsistent cursor position and height. Text now displays correct selection color when window is inactive. Task list markers are now displayed correctly in PDF, HTML, and EPUB. Mermaid diagrams now use correct colors for export. Export to RTF now works as expected. Resolved other bugs and user-interface issues. 3.0 # App icon updated to match the Big Sur style. New export option: DOCX (MS Word). Added support for code highlight within HTML preview. You can now change the font of code blocks in editor. Preview settings now allow you to switch the color theme, font, and header alignment. Colors and HTML preview styles for code blocks updated. QuickLook plugin updated with support for system dark mode. Fixed several issues with HTML export. Code line numbers option removed. Resolved various bugs and user-interface issues. 2.3 # Added numbered lists auto-formatting. Ordered lists will maintain the correct marker number when you insert or delete a list item. Automatic formatting is supported by nested lists as well. All list elements now auto-indent multi-paragraph text items. This change is needed to maintain consistency between Markdown source and HTML preview. Added new settings options for line height, paragraph spacing, and indentation. List insertion shortcuts can now be applied to several lines at once. Added option for displaying code line numbers in HTML preview. Colors and HTML preview styles for code blocks updated. QuickLook plugin updated with new style for code blocks.å Resolved various user-interface issues. 2.2 # Added highlight for header links: # Header [link]. Header labels are now hidden in Navigation view. Mermaid plugin updated to version 8.9.1. Flowchart plugin updated to version 1.14.1. MathJax plugin updated to version 3.1.2. Fixed issue with System font being unavailable in settings. App icon updated. 2.1.5 # Swap lines easily with new shortcuts: ⌥+⌘+↑ and ⌥+⌘+↓. You can now use the Tab/Shift+Tab shortcuts for text indentation. Additional improvements for Navigation panel. Additional under-the-hood updates.
